instructions: Rinse the 1 1/2 cups rice in cold water until the water runs mostly clear, then cook it in a rice cooker or a covered pot. Start the omelettes when the rice is nearly done.
Trim and thinly slice 4 of the green onions.
Crack the 8 eggs into a bowl or jug with a spout. Add 4 tsp fish sauce and the green onions and beat with a fork until the eggs are frothy and there are no streaks of white left.

Pour 1/3 cup of the oil into a wok or an 8-inch skillet and heat it over medium-high until it shimmers and just starts to smoke. You want it at about 375°F, so if you have a thermometer, check it. No thermometer? Dip a chopstick in the egg and then into the oil: it's ready when it sizzles right away.

Pour a quarter of the egg, about 1/2 cup, into the middle of the oil. Stand back a little. It'll puff up and spatter. Cook for about 1 minute without moving it, until the underside is golden brown and the edges are crisp. Lift an edge with a spatula to check.
Flip it and cook the other side for about 1 minute, until it's golden too.
Lift it out and hold it over the pan for a few seconds so the oil drips off, then put it on a plate lined with paper towels.
Cook the other three the same way. Add some of the rest of the oil when the pan looks low, and let it heat up again before each one.
Serve each omelette over a mound of the rice, with the Sriracha on the side.
method_notes: All three beat the eggs with fish sauce, pour them into plenty of very hot oil so they puff and crisp at the edges, fry them about a minute a side and serve them over jasmine rice with chili sauce. Cooking with Nart, the lead, beats one egg per person with 1/2 tsp fish sauce and a chopped green onion and tests the oil with a chopstick dipped in egg. Grantourismo fries two eggs in about 1.5 cm of oil at 375°F, and Saveur adds soy sauce and cornstarch for lacier edges and heats the oil to 410°F. This one makes four two-egg omelettes one after another in the same pan.
